question_text: How many voting members are in the House of Representatives?

why_it_matters.text: The House has 435 members so representation roughly matches population. California gets 52 representatives; Wyoming only gets 1. More people means more voices in the House — unlike the Senate, where Wyoming and California each get exactly 2 senators.

fun_fact.text: The number of representatives in the House grew with the country until 1929. The first House had 65 members in 1789, then expanded after each census — 105, 142, 213, all the way to 435 by 1913. Then Congress passed the Permanent Apportionment Act of 1929, capping the House at 435 forever — even as the U.S. population kept growing.
